question.text: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) are listed exclusively in __________, while Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) are listed on stock exchanges outside the US. Both instruments represent shares of a domestic company traded on foreign exchanges.

answer.text: both the US and European exchanges
any exchange globally including the US

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p56, Depositary Receipts are shares of a local company listed and traded outside the country; they are called ADRs when listed on a US stock exchange such as NYSE, and GDRs when listed outside the USA. Per p57, the mechanics involve a depositary bank holding the underlying shares. The Trap: Candidates often confuse ADRs and GDRs or assume GDRs can be listed in the US. The key distinction per p56 is geographic: ADR = US exchange; GDR = outside US. Note: ADR = American = US exchanges. GDR = Global = non-US exchanges. Both are depositary-receipt mechanisms for trading domestic shares on foreign exchanges.
